title: Choose the visual world for the Mango console
question: The roll assigned The Evidence Docket. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Evidence Docket
options.lineage: forensic case files, chain-of-custody forms, numbered exhibit tags
options.thesis: Every incident is a numbered case; every log record is a numbered exhibit; every agent is a signed entry in the chain of custody. It refuses the dark-dashboard-with-neon-accent this category always ships, and refuses cards-as-structure: the page is a ruled docket, not a deck.
options.viewport: Left: the case register, a dense ruled list of incidents, each row a case number in tabular figures with a sealed severity tag. Right: the open case file on a pale carbon-copy plane, header stamped with status. Below: the investigation, a five-station route diagram of the agents, then FINDINGS, PROBABLE CAUSE with its confidence, and EVIDENCE as numbered exhibits. Clicking a citation in the cause lights its exhibit.
options.risk: A docket reads as costume if the ruling is decorative. It has to be a working table with real tabular figures and real density, or it is just a theme.

raised.raise: Catalogue numbers become typographic identity, not metadata: case and exhibit numbers set as headlines, the way a FAC number is the only headline on the sleeve.
The five-agent pipeline is drawn as a route diagram with interchange nodes at disciplined angles, not five pills in a row.
A row whose status changed holds its marker until it has been seen, rather than silently restyling.
Labels are plain language naming the action, not docket jargon for its own sake.

options.label: The Air-Accident Docket
options.thesis: The report structure Mango already produces, made literal: FINDINGS, then PROBABLE CAUSE, then SAFETY RECOMMENDATIONS, each numbered, each citing its evidence.
options.viewport: The incident as a docket cover sheet; the investigation as a numbered findings list that cannot state a cause without citing the findings above it.
options.risk: It is my top-ranked candidate, which makes it the predictable one: an accident report is the obvious reading of an incident tool, and the roll exists to stop me shipping the obvious. It also skews formal, which fights the dense live-triage half of the brief.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.thesis: The investigation as a route: five stations, disciplined angles, the current station lit.
options.viewport: The agent pipeline as a transit line across the top of the case, the run travelling it.
options.case: Beats the docket on product clarity for the pipeline specifically: a lit route is the clearest possible answer to 'where is this run'. Loses on audience identification, a transit map says city, not incident. Its discipline is donated, not its clothes.
options.risk: Line colours collide with the severity colour system.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse Board
options.thesis: The incident register as a live board: rows are entities, columns never move, changes cascade.
options.viewport: A ruled board of incident rows under fixed columns, severity as row lamps.
options.case: Holds audience identification, an ops status board is genuinely kin to an incident register, and row-identity-on-change is a real idea. Loses on product clarity: per-character flipping on log text is noise, and Mango's list is not a live time-ranked queue.
options.risk: The cascade animation becomes the product.

options.label: Saville Catalogue Sleeve
options.thesis: Every artifact is a catalogue number; colour encodes what words would say.
options.case: Declined: colour-as-label and 'nothing labelled twice' actively hurt a surface scanned at 3am, and fail contrast requirements. Kept: total commitment to the catalogue number as identity, which the docket now carries.

options.label: Boarding Pass and Gate Board
options.thesis: A changed row moves in place and stays lit until noticed.
options.case: Declined: travel ephemera is not this audience's world. Kept: its state discipline, a status change must be noticed, not silently applied.

options.label: Warm Consumer App Surface
options.thesis: Soft-cornered cards on a warm ground, one saturated action colour.
options.case: Declined on both axes: it is the surface every AI build ships, cards-as-page-structure is the lazy container, and a warm orange accent collides head-on with HIGH and CRITICAL severity. Kept: plain-language labels.

options.label: Doujin Event Catalog
options.thesis: Hundreds of stamp-sized cells packed edge to edge, marked by hand.
options.case: Declined: incidents have no thumbnail, so the grid has nothing to pack. Kept: its density courage, do not fear many rows on one screen.

canonCard.label: The Observability Dashboard
canonCard.thesis: Near-black ground, one neon accent, sparklines, stat tiles, a left icon rail. Played straight, at full fidelity, no irony.
canonCard.viewport: Icon rail, filter bar, dense incident table, right drawer for detail.
canonCard.risk: Instantly familiar to every SRE, and instantly forgettable. Also exactly what this category's AI builds converge on.
